findings.text: the added _tree_bytes duplicates tree_size_bytes (reckon/crew/dispatch_launch.py:741), which already owns 'total bytes of the regular files beneath a path, symlinks excluded' and is used by remove_worker_scratch at :871 and imported by reckon/crew/promotion.py:75, promotion_release.py:18 and reckon/crew/routing.py:1733,1915; the only caller _remove_attempt_harness_caches calls _tree_bytes after establishing target is not a symlink (:2645-2647), so the duplicate's extra top-level-symlink branch is unreachable and tree_size_bytes(target) is a drop-in; a second walk implementation in the same module drifts from the one four other modules measure run directories with.

test_a_run_that_*_keeps_every_cache (line 85-93) seeds the fixtures and asserts they are present without invoking any production code, so it passes for every possible implementation of _remove_attempt_harness_caches and cannot redden on any regression; the done_when clause 'a fixture that has not exited keeps everything' is therefore recorded as covered while nothing exercises the exit path's absence.

the path-set assertion compares _remove_attempt_harness_caches' returned paths against ATTEMPT_HARNESS_CACHES, the same constant the function reads to build them, so the two sides move together and the assertion survives any mutation of that constant on its own; only the byte-sum assertion at :138, pinned to the independently seeded _CACHE_FILES sizes, and the presence assertions in test_an_exited_attempt_* at :78 make the file meaningful.
